content: Oseltamivir, marketed as TAMIFLU, should be initiated within 48 hours of the onset of influenza symptoms or after close contact with an infected individual. It can be administered with or without food, but taking it with food may improve tolerability in some patients. For individuals who are unable to swallow capsules, the oral suspension formulation of TAMIFLU is recommended. If the oral suspension is unavailable, the capsules can be opened and mixed with sweetened liquids such as regular or sugar-free chocolate syrup, corn syrup, caramel topping, or light brown sugar dissolved in water. In cases where the appropriate capsule strengths or the oral suspension are not available, a pharmacist can prepare an emergency supply of oral suspension using TAMIFLU 75 mg capsules. For the treatment of influenza in adults and adolescents aged 13 years and older, the recommended oral dose is 75 mg twice daily for 5 days. Patients who cannot swallow capsules may use the oral suspension, where 12.5 mL of the suspension delivers a 75 mg dose. For pediatric patients aged 1 year to 12 years, the recommended oral dose for treating influenza is determined based on body weight, as outlined in Table 1 (not provided here). For infants aged 2 weeks to less than 1 year, the recommended dose is 3 mg/kg administered twice daily for 5 days. For the prophylaxis of influenza in adults and adolescents aged 13 years and older following close contact with an infected individual, the recommended oral dose is 75 mg once daily for at least 10 days. During a community outbreak, the prophylactic dose is also 75 mg once daily. Clinical studies have demonstrated safety and efficacy for up to 6 weeks in immunocompetent patients, with protection lasting as long as the dosing continues. In immunocompromised patients, safety has been established for up to 12 weeks. Patients who cannot swallow capsules may use the oral suspension, where 12.5 mL delivers a 75 mg dose. For pediatric patients aged 1 to 12 years, the recommended prophylactic dose is based on body weight, as detailed in Table 1 (not provided here). Prophylaxis following close contact with an infected individual is recommended for 10 days. During a community outbreak, prophylactic dosing in pediatric patients may be continued for up to 6 weeks.
